titulo: A 2,300-year-old proof you can follow in 40 seconds 🧠
descripcion: Euclid proved the primes never run out with one beautiful trick. Full history of primes, from Euclid to AI, in the linked video.

escenas.texto: Two thousand three hundred years ago, Euclid proved that prime numbers never run out. Here's the whole proof.
Pretend you have a complete list of every prime. Multiply them all, and add one.
Divide that by any prime on your list, and there's always a remainder of one. So it's either a new prime, or built from primes you missed.

visual.pre: divide by any prime on the list

escenas.texto: Try the first six primes and you get thirty thousand and thirty one. That's fifty nine times five hundred nine. Two primes that weren't on the list.
No list can ever be complete. Watch the full video, it's linked right here.
